title: Follow-ups: Frontend portfolio risk panel (PR #66)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #66 (frontend-portfolio-risk-panel), tracked so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: RiskPanel's per-position risk table renders `position_risk_pct` via common/PercentChange, whose green/+ vs. red/- coloring is designed for a gain/loss metric (unrealized_pnl_pct). position_risk_pct is a risk-exposure magnitude that's always >= 0, where higher is worse, not better — confirmed live (browser walkthrough with a mocked 6% breach) that a 2%-rule-breaching row (position_risk_pct=5.00%) still renders its number in green, working against the row's own red breach highlight. Consider a dedicated risk-magnitude display (e.g. red past the 2% threshold, neutral/muted below it) instead of reusing PercentChange for this field.

RiskPanel.tsx defines its own local `formatCurrency` (`$${value.toFixed(2)}`), a near-duplicate of the identical helper already in PositionsTable.tsx, and a third distinct currency format on the same page (PortfolioPage.tsx's StatCards use `toLocaleString(..., {style:'currency'})`, which adds thousands separators the other two lack). Extract one shared currency formatter (e.g. into common/ or a small format utility) so a future change to currency formatting doesn't need to be applied in three places.

The silent-exclusion status note's wording doesn't pluralize correctly when more than one held position is missing from the risk response: 'No risk data available for ZZZZINVALID, TSLA — its price or history couldn't be fetched...' should read 'their price' for a joined multi-ticker list. Minor copy fix.

DataTable's new `getRowStyle` prop got a dedicated Storybook story (`WithFlaggedRow`), but the other new prop, `ariaLabel`, has test coverage only and no story variant. Consider whether it's worth a minimal story (e.g. showing the `aria-label` in the docs/controls panel) to fully match Frontend.md §4's 'every meaningful variant' bar for common/ components, or explicitly note why an accessibility-only prop doesn't need one.

decisions.decision: Built a new dedicated `components/common/RiskPercent` component for position_risk_pct instead of extending PercentChange with a mode/variant, or reusing theme.riskBreach.main directly inline in RiskPanel. It takes the raw value plus the row's own `two_percent_rule_breached` boolean (already on RiskPosition — no re-derivation of the 2% threshold on the frontend) and renders in `riskBreach.main` when breached, `text.secondary` otherwise, with no leading '+' sign (a risk magnitude is never a "gain").
decisions.rationale: Rejected extending PercentChange: its entire contract is sign-driven gain/loss coloring (positive=green/+, negative=red, zero=neutral) plus a leading '+' — bolting an unrelated breached-flag-driven risk mode onto it would mean two independent coloring strategies gated by a mode prop, complicating its single-responsibility tests/stories for a case that shares almost nothing with the gain/loss one. Rejected inlining the color logic directly in RiskPanel.tsx: it's exactly the kind of small, presentational, domain-agnostic (takes a plain number + boolean, no knowledge of 'position'/'portfolio') display primitive Frontend.md's common/ placement test calls out, the same rationale PercentChange itself was built under, so it gets its own component + story + tests rather than being inline JSX in a feature component.

decisions.decision: Consolidated the currency formatter into `utils/format.ts`'s new `formatCurrency`, using the richer `toLocaleString(..., {style:'currency'})` implementation (thousands separators) that PortfolioPage.tsx already had, rather than the plainer `$${value.toFixed(2)}` from RiskPanel.tsx/PositionsTable.tsx. Updated RiskPanel.tsx, PositionsTable.tsx, and PortfolioPage.tsx to import it instead of each defining their own.
decisions.rationale: Standardizing on the richer formatter is strictly better for a finance app (correct thousands-separator display) and never worse, so there was no reason to keep the plainer one or introduce a third hybrid. Scoped the consolidation to the three formatters this task's checklist item actually names (all on the Portfolio page) rather than also touching DashboardPage.tsx's/PositionsGlanceTable.tsx's separate near-identical formatters on the Dashboard page, which are out of this task's stated scope — left as a candidate for a future follow-up rather than scope creep here.

decisions.decision: Fixed pluralization for both halves of the silent-exclusion sentence ('its price' -> 'their price' *and* the previously-unflagged "so it's excluded" -> "so they're excluded") when 2+ tickers are missing, not just the one clause the checklist item quoted.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item's example sentence contains two singular pronouns tied to the same missing-ticker count ('its price' and "it's excluded"); fixing only the first would leave an equally-wrong "so it's excluded" for a 2+-ticker case, which is the same bug the checklist item is about, not a separate one.

decisions.decision: Added a DataTable `WithAriaLabel` Storybook story rather than adding a code comment explaining why `ariaLabel` doesn't need one.
decisions.rationale: `ariaLabel` is a real, documented prop on a common/ component whose only effect (the underlying <table>'s accessible name) is otherwise invisible in Storybook's canvas — a story with it set makes the prop visible/controllable in the docs/controls panel, satisfying Frontend.md §4's 'every meaningful variant' bar the same way WithFlaggedRow does for getRowStyle, rather than carving out an exception for accessibility-only props.
